corrections.reason: Atul Kohli's seminal 1997 article is titled 'Can Democracies Accommodate Ethnic Nationalism?', not 'Ethnic Movements'.

quiz.q: According to the notes, what primarily enabled Indian democracy to survive despite severe socio-economic obstacles?
options: A flexible consensus Constitution that reconciled dominant liberalism with alternative ideological perspectives.
The strict enforcement of a uniform civil code across all religious and linguistic communities.
A rigid constitutional framework that prevented regional movements from challenging the central government.
Rapid industrial modernization that eliminated regional economic disparities shortly after independence.
quiz.why: The Constitution succeeded because it acted as a flexible consensus document, balancing institutional liberalism with alternative viewpoints in Part IV.

quiz.q: How does the Marxist perspective conceptualize the nation, in contrast to liberal and cultural nationalist views?
options: As a natural and spiritual entity that binds individuals across generations through shared cultural consciousness.
As an invented tradition rather than an organic entity, emerging alongside specific socio-economic transformations.
As an evolutionary political community developing naturally as traditional societies undergo modernization and secularization.
As a permanent biological collective rooted in primordial attachments and ancient linguistic loyalties.
quiz.why: Marxists regard nationalism as an invented tradition, whereas liberals link it to modernization and cultural nationalists view it as natural and spiritual.

quiz.q: What paradox does Atul Kohli highlight regarding the relationship between democracy and ethnic movements in India?
options: Centralized power suppresses ethnic mobilization, whereas federal devolution inevitably leads to national disintegration.
Economic modernization eliminates ethnic demands, but electoral politics artificially revives ancient regional grievances.
Democratic politics stimulates ethnic mobilization, yet democratic accommodation provides the only enduring solution.
Excessive state force permanently resolves ethnic conflicts, whereas democratic negotiation only delays violent secession.
quiz.why: Kohli argues that democratic politics triggers ethnic mobilization, but peaceful democratic negotiation remains the only viable mechanism to resolve it.

quiz.q: According to the notes, why is regionalism considered a developmental crisis rather than an inherent threat to national integration?
options: It arises primarily from foreign interference seeking to destabilize border states and weaken national defense.
It stems from uneven regional development and neglect, which can be effectively addressed through power devolution.
It inevitably demands complete secession from the Union unless suppressed by strong centralized armed forces.
It is an ideological movement aimed at replacing constitutional democracy with monistic sovereign state control.
quiz.why: Regionalism stems from uneven growth and neglect rather than inherent hostility to national unity, warranting democratic devolution of power.
